/-!
# Erdős Problem 544

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/544](https://www.erdosproblems.com/544)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos544

/--
Show that
$$R(3,k+1)-R(3,k)\to\infty$$
as $k\to \infty$.

A problem of Erdős and Sós.
This problem is #8 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_544.parts.i :
    Tendsto (fun k : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 3 (k + 1) : ℝ) -
      (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 3 k : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Similarly, prove or disprove that
$$R(3,k+1)-R(3,k)=o(k).$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_544.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    (fun k : ℕ ↦ (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 3 (k + 1) : ℝ) -
      (SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey 3 k : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun k : ℕ ↦ (k : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos544

reformulations.difference: The supplementary literature source, Zhu–Xu–Radziszowski equation (5), asks whether Δ_s/s → 0 for Δ_s = R(3,s) − R(3,s−1). Lean uses the forward difference R(3,k+1) − R(3,k) = o(k).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Set s = k+1. Shifting a sequence by one preserves its limit at infinity. For k ≥ 1, k ≤ k+1 ≤ 2k, so little-o relative to k is equivalent to little-o relative to k+1. With an eventually nonzero denominator, little-o is equivalent to the ratio tending to zero. This equivalence was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Both declarations match the Erdős–Sós questions stated in the literature. Lean checks verified the standard Ramsey-number characterization, R(3,0)=0 and R(3,1)=1, the quantifier meaning of divergence to +∞, and both statements' equivalence to the paper's formulations. The real-valued subtraction and inclusion of k=0 cause no defect. Access limitation: https://www.erdosproblems.com/544 consistently returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers. Exact mathematical wording was therefore corroborated using the research paper above. The independent problem database records #544 as open, but the live webpage's latest per-part status and remarks could not be checked directly.
